subject: Hosted streaming probe scope + schedule — p95/p99 targets vs incumbent
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@novushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + proposed probe scope (p95/p99 streaming + throughput)

Hi Susan / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Good conversation; appreciate you walking us through the production profile. Per request, here’s a concise probe scope we propose to validate p95/p99 end-to-end latency on Redwood Hosted vs your incumbent provider (what you described as "BatchEndpointX"). High level:

- Objective: measure realistic streaming tail (p95/p99) and throughput under representative concurrency patterns for your chat agent flows.
- Key success criteria (provisional): p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 450ms for single-turn chat responses under median token lengths (avg 120 tokens); streaming chunk latency target: first-chunk p50 < 80ms.
- Workload: mixed-length messages from your sample traffic (attached), including 5% long-form (>=1024 tokens), 80% short (<=128 tokens), 15% medium.
- Concurrency envelope: run tests at 1, 5, 20, 50 concurrent connections from a single region (US East) to compare routing/scale behavior.
- Throughput checks: measure sustained sustained throughput per connection and aggregate across gateways to footprint GPU util and tail behavior.
- Warm/cold cache scenarios: 30-minute sustained warm run + abrupt cold-start spikes to emulate traffic bursts after inactivity.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Confirm you can share a sanitized sample (we received novus_traffic_sample_v2.jsonl — thanks), 2) Pick a three-hour test window next week where we can run parallel probes, 3) We’ll deliver a measurement plan + Jupyter workbook and the exact test harness commands.

I’ve attached a draft measurement plan and a short testing checklist. Can you confirm if the provisional p95/p99 targets above align with your expectations or whether your procurement gate requires different thresholds?

Thanks —

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.ai] | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: p95_p99_measurement_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), novus_traffic_sample_v2.jsonl (traffic sample)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + proposed probe scope (p95/p99 streaming + throughput)

Jonas / Ben —

Couple technical clarifications before we lock a window:

1) Model configuration parity: we need Novus to confirm the exact model/variant used at the incumbent (quantization, context length, batching settings). If they run aggressive batching at the provider, that can mask per-request tail.

2) Streaming protocol: are you using full SSE streaming (chunked deltas) or simulated chunked responses on top of non-streaming endpoints? We should measure first-byte latency and inter-chunk spacing separately.

3) KV cache / prefix caching: confirm approximate cache hit rate for the prod traffic. For warm-run vs cold-run distinction, we’ll simulate 80% cache-hit and 20% cold requests in the mixed traffic to reflect 'session continuation' behavior.

4) Measurement hooks: we’ll instrument both client-side RTT (browser to edge) and server-side processing times. To compare fairly vs BatchEndpointX we need a common synthetic harness that replays the same timestamps and tokenization.

I’m attaching the minimal harness commands (in the spreadsheet) and a shell script to reproduce the load. If we can get model runtime config by EOD Wednesday I can finalize the test commands.

--Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

From: Susan Park <susan.park@novushealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@novushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + proposed probe scope (p95/p99 streaming + throughput)

Thanks Jonas / Camila —

This looks good and aligns with what the SREs care about. Quick answers:

- Incumbent config: They run a 16-bit quantized variant with custom batching window (100ms agg, up to 8 requests per batch). We will request the exact batching telemetry but expect batching to reduce observed p95 for high throughput bursts.
- Streaming: Our prod conversational UX uses SSE with incremental tokens; first-chunk latency is the main metric for end-user perceived responsiveness.
- Cache: Session-level prefix caching is around 65% hit rate in normal traffic; spikes drop it to ~30%.

We can share the provider’s endpoint config and a small telemetry excerpt by EOD Thursday. For scheduling, our preferred window is Friday 8/7 10:00–13:00 EDT (we want morning US East). That works for our SRE and PM.

We accept the provisional success criteria you listed as a starting point. If Redwood can demonstrate parity or improvement on p95/p99 AND provide a recommended mitigation plan for cold-start tails (e.g., prewarm, lightweight fallback variant), procurement will be happy to consider a pilot.

Also appreciate the measurement plan — I’ll upload the telemetry snippet and the provider config to the shared Drive link in a bit.

Best,

Susan Park
Director, AI Products — Novus Health
Susan.Park@novushealth.com

Susan / Tom —

Great — thanks for the quick alignment and for pulling telemetry. Sequencing / next steps from our side:

1) Jon + Camila will run the scripted probes on Friday 8/7 10:00–13:00 EDT (we will be in US East region).
2) We’ll run Redwood Hosted and the incumbent side-by-side using the same harness and report per-request client RTT, first-chunk latency, inter-chunk gaps, p95/p99, and GPU utilization.
3) Deliverable: consolidated results and a short decision memo (1 page) within 48 hours of the window; detailed logs and Jupyter workbook in the shared Drive.

Action items:
- Novus: upload provider config + telemetry to Drive (Susan) — due Thu EOD (8/6).
- Redwood: finalize measurement plan and test scripts (Camila) — due Thu EOD (8/6).
- Everyone: confirm Friday window — confirmed by email thread.

If we hit the targets, next commercial step we’ll recommend is a two-week pilot on dedicated capacity to validate sustained throughput under real traffic patterns.

Looking forward to the run —

Ben Carter
